clinicalPearls: SPG47 is an autosomal recessive, early-onset complicated HSP caused by biallelic mutations in AP4B1, the gene for the beta-1 subunit of adaptor protein complex 4 (AP-4).
It is one of the four AP-4 deficiency syndromes, together with SPG50 (AP4M1), SPG51 (AP4E1) and SPG52 (AP4S1), which are clinically almost indistinguishable.
Neonatal or infantile hypotonia characteristically evolves into a progressive spastic tetraplegia in which the legs are affected more than the arms.
Severe intellectual disability with absent or very limited speech is typical.
Postnatal (progressive) microcephaly is characteristic, so head circumference may be normal at birth.
Epilepsy is common and seizures are often triggered by fever; a cheerful demeanour with stereotypic bouts of laughter is frequently described.
MRI typically shows a thin corpus callosum, reduced white-matter volume and ventriculomegaly.
Progressive foot contractures, a spastic gait and eventual loss of independent ambulation are usual.
reference.pathophysiology: SPG47 is caused by loss-of-function mutations in AP4B1 on chromosome 1p13.2, which encodes the beta-1 subunit of the heterotetrameric adaptor protein complex 4 (AP-4). AP-4 operates at the trans-Golgi network, selecting transmembrane cargo — notably the autophagy protein ATG9A and AMPA-type glutamate receptors — into vesicles for correct somatodendritic and axonal delivery. When any AP-4 subunit is absent the complex cannot assemble, ATG9A is mistrafficked and accumulates at the trans-Golgi, autophagosome biogenesis and axonal cargo sorting are impaired, and the longest corticospinal axons degenerate; this shared molecular lesion explains why mutations in the four different subunits (AP4B1, AP4M1, AP4E1, AP4S1) converge on a single AP-4 deficiency phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: SPG50 (AP4M1), SPG51 (AP4E1) and SPG52 (AP4S1) — the allelic AP-4 deficiency syndromes
Spastic-diplegic cerebral palsy, which is non-progressive
Angelman syndrome — shares the happy demeanour, laughter and seizures
SPG11 and SPG15 — complicated HSP with thin corpus callosum
Rett syndrome and other developmental encephalopathies with regression
Mitochondrial or other metabolic encephalopathies of infancy
additionalInvestigations: MRI brain to demonstrate thin corpus callosum, white-matter loss and ventriculomegaly
Molecular genetic testing (exome or an HSP / AP-4 gene panel covering AP4B1, AP4M1, AP4E1, AP4S1)
Serial head-circumference measurement to document progressive microcephaly
Neurodevelopmental assessment and swallowing / feeding evaluation
Metabolic screen to exclude treatable mimics
redFlags: Developmental regression or loss of previously acquired skills
Progressive contractures compromising posture and mobility
reference.prognosis: SPG47 is a severe, life-long condition: most affected children become non-ambulant, remain non-verbal or minimally verbal and require full-time care, although progression of the neurological deficits is generally slow.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosis as cerebral palsy because the early hypotonic-to-spastic evolution can look static if not followed over time
Confusion with Angelman syndrome owing to the laughter, happy affect and epilepsy
Assuming a normal birth head circumference excludes the disorder, since the microcephaly is postnatal
Testing only AP4B1 and missing an allelic AP-4 subunit gene
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Symptomatic antispasticity therapy with baclofen or tizanidine, escalating to intrathecal baclofen for severe spasticity, plus botulinum toxin for focal spasticity and contracture prevention
Anti-seizure medication for epilepsy, with prompt antipyretic treatment given the tendency to fever-triggered seizures
Physiotherapy, stretching, supportive seating, orthoses and orthopaedic care with hip surveillance for the spastic tetraplegic child
Swallowing and feeding assessment with nutritional support and enteral feeding where aspiration risk is significant
Developmental and communication support including augmentative and alternative communication for severe intellectual disability and absent speech
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and carrier testing of relatives
Multidisciplinary paediatric neurology, rehabilitation, respiratory and complex-care or palliative input
